schema_query: Do federal judges appointed by different Presidents (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic) differ in their voting tendencies on immigration injunction cases? Do Trump-appointed judges tend to be more supportive of Trump administration immigration policies compared to judges appointed by other Republican or Democratic presidents?

columns.name: case_name
columns.definition: The name of the court case or lawsuit.
columns.rationale: Identifies the specific legal dispute being analyzed.

pending_values.value: A.S.R. v. Donald J. Trump, et al.
AMERICAN GATEWAYS, et al., v. U.S. DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE, et al.
Amica Center for Immigrant Rights, et al. v. U.S. Department of Justice, et al.
ANGELICA S., et al. v. U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES, et al.
Darwin Antonio Arevalo Millan v. Donald J. Trump, et al.
Barbara, et al. v. Donald J. Trump, President of the United States, in his official capacity, et al.

columns.name: judge_name
columns.definition: The name of the federal judge presiding over the case and issuing the ruling.
columns.rationale: Crucial for identifying the individual judge to analyze their voting patterns and appointment background.

columns.name: appointing_president
columns.definition: The U.S. President who appointed the presiding judge.
columns.rationale: Directly addresses the core independent variable of the query (Trump vs. other Republican vs. Democratic appointees).

columns.name: challenged_policy
columns.definition: The specific immigration policy, executive order, or administrative rule challenged in the case.
columns.rationale: Allows researchers to categorize the types of immigration policies being contested and see if voting patterns differ by policy type.

columns.name: injunction_ruling_outcome
columns.definition: The court's decision regarding the requested preliminary injunction or temporary restraining order.
columns.rationale: Measures the dependent variable of the query (the judge's voting tendency on immigration injunctions).

columns.name: supports_administration_position
columns.definition: Indicates whether the judge's ruling ultimately supported the Trump administration's legal position or policy enforcement.
columns.rationale: Directly answers whether the judge's voting tendency is supportive of the administration's policies.
